name: Andrew 'Boz' Bosworth
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Facebook in January 2006 as one of its first ~15 engineers and developed the Facebook News Feed, which launched later that year and became a defining feature of the platform.
early_history_summary: Bosworth grew up on a farm in Saratoga, California and learned to program through the 4-H agricultural youth program. He attended Harvard University, where he met Mark Zuckerberg while serving as a teaching fellow in an AI course. After graduating cum laude in 2004, he worked at Microsoft on Visio for nearly two years before joining Facebook in early 2006 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Grew up on a farm in Saratoga, California; involved in 4-H agricultural programs as a child. Family financial status not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Harvard, Silicon Valley native, early Facebook, Zuckerberg connection
evidence_summary: Bosworth grew up in Santa Clara County, California, at the heart of Silicon Valley, and had early access to computers via an Apple IIe at home. He attended Harvard University where he met Mark Zuckerberg as a teaching fellow in an AI course, creating a direct personal connection to the founder of Facebook. After graduating in 2004 and a brief stint at Microsoft, he joined Facebook as one of its first ~15 engineers in January 2006 at age 24, where he built the News Feed. The combination of Harvard's institutional pipeline, Silicon Valley geographic proximity, and the social media structural wave created a powerful early-advantage stack.
starting_point: Born and raised on a farm in Saratoga, California (Santa Clara County); family background beyond farming not documented.
current_position: CTO of Meta Platforms and Head of Reality Labs; also commissioned as Lieutenant Colonel in U.S. Army Reserve in 2025.

trajectory.event: Graduated cum laude from Harvard University with a BS in computer science.
Joined Facebook as one of its first ~15 engineers and developed the Facebook News Feed.
Led Facebook's transition from desktop to mobile advertising, overseeing creation of mobile ad products.
Transitioned to VP of augmented and virtual reality at Facebook.
Became CTO of Meta Platforms while continuing to lead Reality Labs.
Commissioned as Lieutenant Colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve to advise Detachment 201.

name: Noam Shazeer
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Google in 2000 as an early employee and implemented the search engine's spelling corrector in his first two weeks, then developed the PHIL algorithm which became the core of Google AdSense.
early_history_summary: Shazeer was born in Philadelphia to an Orthodox Jewish family; his grandparents escaped the Holocaust. He won a gold medal with a perfect score at the International Mathematical Olympiad in 1994 as a member of the US team. He studied math and computer science at Duke University on the prestigious Angier B. Duke Memorial Scholarship from 1994 to 1998, then briefly attended Berkeley's graduate program before leaving to join Google in 2000.
family_context_summary: Born to an Orthodox Jewish family in Philadelphia; grandparents escaped the Holocaust into the Soviet Union before emigrating to the USA. Father Dov Shazeer was a math teacher who became an engineer; mother was a homemaker. Sister was ordained as a rabbi.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a math teacher who became an engineer, providing a household with strong mathematical and technical orientation that likely influenced Shazeer's early development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IMO gold medal perfect score, Duke Angier B. Duke Scholarship, Google early employee, mathematical prodigy
evidence_summary: Shazeer demonstrated exceptional mathematical ability early, winning a gold medal with a perfect score at the 1994 International Mathematical Olympiad as a US team member. His father, a math teacher turned engineer, provided a domain-relevant home environment. He attended Duke University on the prestigious Angier B. Duke Memorial Scholarship and won Putnam Competition prizes. At Google, where he joined in 2000 as an early employee, he was mentored by Jeff Dean and quickly implemented the spelling corrector and co-developed the PHIL algorithm that powered AdSense. His grandparents' Holocaust survival and immigrant background created a context of urgency and educational emphasis.
starting_point: Born in Philadelphia to an Orthodox Jewish family; father was a math teacher turned engineer, mother a homemaker; grandparents were Holocaust survivors who emigrated via the Soviet Union and Israel.
current_position: AI researcher at OpenAI as of 2026; previously co-led Google Gemini and co-founded Character.AI; estimated to have netted $750M-$1B from Google's Character.AI licensing deal.

trajectory.event: Won a gold medal with perfect score at the International Mathematical Olympiad as a member of the US team.
Graduated from Duke University with a BS in math and computer science on the Angier B. Duke Memorial Scholarship.
Joined Google as an early employee; implemented the spelling corrector and developed the PHIL algorithm powering AdSense.
Co-authored the seminal paper 'Attention Is All You Need,' introducing the transformer architecture.
Co-founded Character.AI with Daniel de Freitas after Google refused to release their Meena chatbot.
Returned to Google to co-lead Gemini as part of a $2.7B deal; estimated to net $750M-$1B from Character.AI stake.
Left Google to join OpenAI; elected to the National Academy of Engineering.

name: John D. Musa

name: Matt Rogers
milestone_by_age_26: Became Senior Manager of iPod and iPhone Software at Apple in January 2007, having been one of the first engineers on the original iPhone team; by age 26 he had contributed to 10 generations of iPod and the first iPhone.
early_history_summary: Rogers grew up in Gainesville, Florida and had a Mac Plus at age three, developing a lifelong passion for Apple. He flew to Cupertino at age 13 and told his grandparents he would work at Apple. He earned BS and MS degrees in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Carnegie Mellon University (2001-2005), then joined Apple as an engineering intern in 2004, quickly rising to Senior Manager of iPod and iPhone Software by January 2007.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Gainesville, Florida; had a Mac Plus at age three and flew to Cupertino with grandparents at age 13. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU ECE, Apple internship, iPod/iPhone software, Tony Fadell mentorship, early computer access
evidence_summary: Rogers had early computer access (Mac Plus at age three) and a deep childhood passion for Apple, visiting Cupertino at 13. He attended Carnegie Mellon University for BS and MS in Electrical and Computer Engineering (2001-2005), a top-tier engineering pipeline that led directly to an Apple internship in 2004. He rose rapidly to Senior Manager of iPod and iPhone Software by January 2007, working alongside Tony Fadell as a mentor and collaborator. His direct immersion in consumer electronics product development on the iPhone—one of the most consequential product launches in history—constituted deep domain proximity at a young age.
starting_point: Grew up in Gainesville, Florida; had a Mac Plus at age three and visited Apple HQ at age 13; family background not documented beyond this.
current_position: CEO and co-founder of Mill, a food waste prevention technology company; also founder of Incite.org, a values-based investment fund.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Carnegie Mellon University with BS and MS in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
Became Senior Manager of iPod and iPhone Software at Apple; one of the first engineers on the original iPhone.
Co-founded Nest Labs with Tony Fadell; launched the Nest Learning Thermostat.
Nest Labs acquired by Google for $3.2 billion.
Founded Incite.org, a values-based investment fund for climate solutions.
Co-founded Mill, a food waste prevention technology company.

name: Sebastian Raschka
category: AI researcher and author (Python Machine Learning)
milestone_by_age_26: Published 'Python Machine Learning' in September 2015 at age 24, a widely recognized and translated machine learning textbook that became one of the most popular practical ML references.
early_history_summary: Raschka studied at the University of Würzburg in Germany before completing his PhD in Computational Biology at Michigan State University. While a PhD candidate, he authored 'Python Machine Learning,' which was published by Packt Publishing in September 2015 and was subsequently translated into German, Japanese, Italian, Chinese, Korean, and Russian. The book was named a Notable Book by Computing Reviews in 2016.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Raschka studied at the University of Würzburg in Germany before pursuing his PhD in the United States.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ML education, open source, GitHub, Python Machine Learning book, Packt Publishing
evidence_summary: Raschka's early advantage appears largely self-created rather than inherited. He leveraged the rising machine learning wave and open-source community engagement (GitHub, mlxtend library) to build a reputation as a practical ML educator. His PhD candidacy at Michigan State University provided institutional backing, though it is not a top-tier AI lab. The publication of 'Python Machine Learning' at age 24 demonstrated deep domain knowledge and the ability to synthesize complex topics, but no family financial platform, parental domain expertise, or elite institutional pipeline was documented in reviewed sources.

name: Joel Spolsky
category: Software entrepreneur and writer (Stack Overflow, Fog Creek)
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from Yale University summa cum laude in computer science in 1991 and joined Microsoft as a program manager on the Excel team, where he designed Excel Basic and drove the Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) strategy.
early_history_summary: Spolsky was born in Albuquerque, New Mexico and started programming in 1978 at age 13 on an IBM-360 mainframe at the UNM Computer Center. His family moved to Israel when he was 15, where he completed high school and served in the Israeli Paratroopers Brigade. He co-founded Kibbutz Hanaton before returning to the US for college, attending the University of Pennsylvania for a year before transferring to Yale, where he graduated summa cum laude in computer science in 1991. He immediately joined Microsoft's Excel team as a program manager.
family_context_summary: Born to Jewish parents in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Family moved to Israel when he was 15. He served in the Israeli military (Paratroopers Brigade) and was a founder of Kibbutz Hanaton. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His family moved to Israel, suggesting an internationally mobile household, but no parental domain expertise is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yale summa cum laude, Microsoft Excel team, VBA design, early mainframe access, Israeli military service
evidence_summary: Spolsky started programming at 13 on an IBM-360 mainframe at the University of New Mexico, giving him early access to computing resources that were relatively rare in 1978. He attended Yale University, graduating summa cum laude in computer science in 1991, which placed him directly into Microsoft's Excel team as a program manager. At Microsoft, he designed Excel Basic and drove the VBA strategy—a material contribution to one of the world's most widely used software products. His Israeli military service and international move at 15 created formative adversity and independence. No family financial platform or parental domain expertise was documented.
starting_point: Born to Jewish parents in Albuquerque, New Mexico; family moved to Israel when he was 15; served in Israeli Paratroopers Brigade and co-founded Kibbutz Hanaton before returning to the US for college.
current_position: Co-founder of HASH; former CEO of Stack Overflow (2010-2019); resides on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. Stack Overflow was sold in June 2021 for $1.8 billion.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Yale summa cum laude in CS; joined Microsoft as program manager on Excel team, designing Excel Basic and VBA strategy.
Left Microsoft; moved to New York City and worked at Viacom and Juno Online Services.
Founded Fog Creek Software and launched the influential 'Joel on Software' blog.
Co-founded Stack Overflow with Jeff Atwood, creating the largest online Q&A community for programmers.
Launched Trello at Fog Creek, a Kanban-inspired project management tool.
Trello acquired by Atlassian for $425 million.
Stack Overflow sold for $1.8 billion; Spolsky stepped down as chairman.
